complete_chain_observations: Existing ReskillableRegistryHandler.registerTraits actually constructs TraitSidestep. Constructor binds agility, default cost10, agility26/defense20 requirements and registers this instance on event bus only on physical client. Trait/Unlockable obtains config and actual parent skill. This subscription is separate from PlayerData.forEachEventHandler ability dispatch and occurs without an explicit enabled guard in Sidestep. OnKeyDown later checks unlocked membership and not sneaking; no isEnabled check there. Existing disabled/unknown profile rules not changed.

Existing ClientProxy key-binding registration plus newly read KeyBindings opens actual GuiSkills; full remainder GuiSkills click opens GuiSkillInfo. Skill-info hover computes not-unlocked and enough-points; left click sends MessageUnlockUnlockable. Registered SERVER handler obtains current context player, registry skill/unlockable, checks not already unlocked, points, matchStats and cancelable Pre, then PlayerSkillInfo.unlock subtracts cost/adds object and calls onUnlock; Post follows. saveAndSync is after conditional, so rejected purchase can sync unchanged. Existing MessageDataSync delivers included unlock registry keys into current local profile; that same isUnlocked(this) is input gate. Sender not arbitrary abstract callback. No parent-skill validation/unknown-ID robustness or survival-economy guarantee added.

onKeyDown returns while cd>0, otherwise dereferences current mc.player/profile without explicit null guard and skips locked/sneaking. It does not inspect which key generated event, event press/release state, currentScreen or a release edge. If left key is currently held, stores global ClientTickHandler.ticksInGame into leftDown, compares new-old<4 and calls dodge(left); else right analog. Left wins when both held. No >=0 bound or first-sample initialized flag; default last values0. Timestamp is stored before dodge checks, so failed motion attempt can prime another held-key event. This is event sampling, not proved two distinct presses.

dodge requires not flying, onGround, moveForward<0 and sprint key physically down; input caller already checks unlocked/not sneaking/cd. It computes yaw-facing horizontal unit vector, cross with vertical sign for side and scales1.25. Writes motionX/motionY/motionZ absolutely (Y0), then cd20. No target, damage cancellation, immunity interval, resistance lookup, server request, reply or motion rollback is coded in this local path. Public dodge itself lacks unlocked/sneak/cd gate, but only actual internal caller observed; no external misuse claimed.

Reused ClientTickHandler END increments ticksInGame only if no GUI or GUI does not pause. Sidestep.clientTick independently decrements cd>0 on every delivered END event, without checking screen/world/player/eligibility. Thus if END events are delivered while a pausing screen freezes ticksInGame, recharge can finish while last-input difference stays small. Native event delivery frequency under pause not inspected, so state conditional, not reproduced timing exploit. Both clocks are session objects/fields with no shown world-change reset; leftDown/rightDown andcd have no per-player dimension identity or explicit death/lock clear.

Trait itself subscribes RenderGameOverlayEvent.Post ALL. If player not flying, width=min(int((cd-partialTicks)*2),40); positive width draws fixed gray track and white remaining bar via Gui.drawRect. At cd0 width nonpositive and bar suppressed; no input timestamps cleared. HUD does not require currently unlocked/enabled and has no null-player guard. Flight hides bar while cooldown continues, not a reset; there is no server feedback receipt. Buffer/color requests inspected only, no visual/game/audio execution.

Full cached source search finds MessageDodge only in class/registration, no new MessageDodge or other local gameplay sender. Empty payload is registered SERVER; handler schedules, resolves sender then schedules addExhaustion0.3. It neither checks trait/CD/movement nor sets movement nor confirms action. Without actual sender cannot attribute fatigue spending to local dodge. Public external integration may send it, but this batch proves none. Not an extra packet mechanism or closed server movement-validation chain.
